IV THERAPY & WELLNESS · 5 MIN READ

How Medical IV Vitamin & Hydration Therapy Supports Immunity, Energy & Recovery.

Written by Dr. Michael Le Roux · Family Medicine Specialist at 21 Langverwacht Road, Kuils River.

← Back to All Care Blogs
Author: Dr. Michael Le Roux (MB ChB, MMed Fam Med, PG Dip Palliative Med) Category: IV Therapy & Wellness Reading Time: 5 min read

When your body is fighting off a viral infection, recovering from severe dehydration, or experiencing prolonged work burnout, oral supplements and water alone can take days to restore cellular balance. Medical intravenous (IV) vitamin and hydration therapy delivers sterile fluids, electrolytes, vitamins, and antioxidants directly into the bloodstream for 100% bioavailability—bypassing digestive absorption limits when your body needs rapid replenishment.

Why Intravenous Nutrient Delivery Works Faster

When we take high-dose vitamins orally—especially Vitamin C, Magnesium, and B-complex vitamins—absorption in the gastrointestinal tract is naturally limited by gut transport mechanisms and stomach acidity. During periods of acute illness, gastroenteritis, or stress, gut absorption drops even further. An intravenous infusion allows precise, doctor-prescribed concentrations of nutrients to reach your tissues immediately while simultaneously restoring intravascular fluid volume.

Who Benefits Most from Clinical IV Therapy?

  • Dehydration & Acute Recovery: Rapid fluid and electrolyte restoration after stomach bugs, heat exhaustion, fever, or viral illness.
  • Immune System Support: High-dose Vitamin C, Zinc Sulphate, and B-complex infusions during winter cold and flu season to support white blood cell function and shorten recovery times.
  • Fatigue, Burnout & Migraines: Magnesium, Vitamin B12, and B6 support to calm neuromuscular tension, ease recurrent headaches, and restore cellular energy production.
  • Athletic & Muscle Recovery: Targeted 1-litre electrolyte and amino acid rehydration for runners, cyclists, and active individuals across Kuils River and surrounds.
Clinical Safety First: Doctor-Supervised Infusions

At our Kuils River family practice, IV therapy is never treated as a one-size-fits-all retail drip. Every infusion begins with a clinical check of your medical history, blood pressure, heart rate, and oxygen saturation before your drip is administered in our calm treatment suite.

What to Expect During Your Visit

Most clinical IV sessions take between 35 and 45 minutes. After a brief medical screening with Dr. Michael Le Roux, Dr. Danielle Strydom, or Dr. Rhiyaan Smith, you will relax in a comfortable treatment chair while your infusion is carefully monitored. Patients can return to work or daily activities immediately afterwards feeling hydrated and refreshed.
